title: Fallen Survey Line
description: A surviving foot and three split shaft drums along one fall line, ending in a broken cushion capital.

review.notes: New budget round 1 of 2: rejected. Fixed: the pieces now reuse the approved column's flutes and plinth, the foot keeps its torus and plinth, and there are small chips in the turf. Still failing: (1) silhouette/style: the drums stand on end side by side in a straight row on one oval turf patch, like coins on a shelf (hero, turn_020, turn_245), not a column that fell along one line. (2) form_detail 6: the break faces are crumpled triangle facets (closeup_base upper left, right), one drum is a clean, unbroken cylinder with a single thin crack (closeup_base centre), and the flutes on the lying drums read as stacked convex rings. (3) the capital is a square slab with a round disc stuck on its face (closeup left), not a recognisable broken cushion capital. (4) material/defects: the stone has the old dark marble-like blotches; the turf is a flat oval disc with a hard edge. Fix: lay the drums on their sides along one fall line from the foot, rotated and partly sunk into the soil, with gaps; give the breaks a conchoidal fracture with a few large planes; make the capital a tilted cushion echinus under its abacus with one corner broken off; use the approved column's weathering; blend the turf edge into the ground.
